title: Automated model switch incident — containment, telemetry rewrite, and operational hardening
creator: Priya Desai
description: Summary: During an automated model swap to a newer quantized variant on 2026-02-24 we observed a reproducible degradation that affected tail-latency and prediction confidence for a subset of requests. The swap triggered a subtle KV cache mismatch combined with a kernel selection path that amplifies off-by-one attention behavior on longer prefix distributions. This ticket tracks discrete follow-ups: containment primitives (quarantine proxy and lineage pinning), a telemetry rewrite to capture request lineage and KV keyspace drift, a set of synthetic litmus checks for future swaps, and small runtime hardening changes to the auto-rollback heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine proxy implemented and configurable per-release: can opt-in traffic quarantine that routes suspect requests to a safe variant within 1 minute of activation.
Request lineage token propagated end-to-end and visible in trace logs and ingestion pipeline (dataplane + control plane).
KV cache version pinning added to model descriptors with compatibility check that blocks swaps if mismatch detected during dry-run.
Telemetry pipeline updated to store sampled full KV metadata for 0.1% of requests and expose KV-drift alerting pages on Console.
Three synthetic litmus suites added to CI: long-prefix attention suite, quantized-kernel validation, and per-tenant latency spike simulation. All must pass before automatic traffic ramp to >10%.
Auto-rollback heuristic updated to use hysteresis windows and lineage-aware aggregation so rollbacks do not amplify noisy transient spikes.
updates: 2026-02-25 | Priya Desai: Initial triage summary posted to #infra-incidents and linked the run-of-record. Observed pattern: 95th/99th latency divergence and low-confidence ratings concentrated on requests with prefix length >1024 tokens. Opened this follow-up ticket to coordinate engineering and telemetry teams.

2026-02-26 | Liam Chen: Reproduced locally with synthetic workload. Root cause hypothesis: KV cache key indexing used model-variant-specific namespace; new variant introduced a minor tokenization difference which caused KV cache coldness and forced fallback to full attention kernels increasing latency nonlinearly.
2026-02-28 | SRE Team (note): Deployed temporary traffic quarantine (manual) by routing 100% of affected tenant requests to the prior model. No additional customer-facing incidents after quarantine.
2026-03-02 | Data Eng: Implemented lineage token draft in the dataplane; initial traces show lineage missing in 30% of retried paths. Need more robust propagation through retry/queue layers.

2026-03-04 | Runtime Team: Prototype KV version pinning in model descriptor; runs in dry-run flag mode. Observed two additional variants that would have been blocked by pinning — indicates broad utility.

2026-03-08 | PM Review (Ava Martinez): Prioritized quarantine proxy and telemetry ingestion as P0. Agreed on blocking rule for auto-swap when KV pin check fails in dry-run. Asked for rollout plan by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 | Liam Chen: Completed quarantine proxy MVP (config via runtime policy). Manual test: flip-on quarantines within 40s and routes to warm fallback variant. Pushed PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4382.

2026-03-12 | Priya Desai: Telemetry sampling pipeline PR opened to store KV metadata with lineage token. Created dashboards and an alert rule on KV keyspace divergence threshold (0.8 Jaccard index drop).
TODO: add metrics after production rollout of quarantine proxy and telemetry update (expected 2026-03-15).
notes: Decision log: We prioritized quarantine proxy over immediate changes to kernel selection because it yields a fast operational lever with minimal code-path risk.
Trade-offs: Quarantine proxy increases tail routing complexity and slightly increases management surface. We accept a small operational cost in exchange for faster containment capability.
Long-term: Consider moving KV keyspace into versioned shards to avoid cross-variant collisions. This is an architectural effort and will be captured as a separate initiative.
Communication: Send an internal blameless postmortem summary to GTM and customer success with suggested tenant-level mitigations and an offer for priority rollback assistance for impacted customers.
